title: Protocol for constructing a hierarchical host-guest supramolecular self-assembly system in water
protocol: Dilute guest molecule aqueous solution according to the experimental requirements.
Set measuring mode in UVProbe software to absorbance.
Set slit width to 2.0 nm.
Set scan wavelengths from 250 nm to 800 nm.
Set scan speed to fast.
Set sampling interval to 0.5 nm.
Control test temperature at a constant 25°C as required.
Place two cells containing background solvent into the sample stage.
Perform "auto zero" and establish baseline using UVProbe software.
Ensure observed absorption value at 800 nm is within ±0.002 before testing.
Handle quartz sample cells with care to avoid skin scratches from broken cells.
Replace test cell with guest molecule aqueous solution and start scanning for UV-vis spectra.
Gradually add a trace volume of concentrated host molecule aqueous solution or dispersion into the test cell to achieve calculated molar ratios (e.g., 1:0.1, 1:0.2... up to 1:1.5).
Obtain UV-vis spectra after ensuring sample solutions are thoroughly mixed.
Monitor self-assembly system for any changes during measurements.
Prepare a D2O solution of the guest molecule according to step 2 in Part: Preparation of the aqueous solution of the guest molecule.
Calculate the required volume of the D2O solution of the guest molecule.
Ensure the concentration of the D2O solution of the guest molecule is at least 1 × 10–3 M due to sensitivity considerations for 1H-NMR.
Prepare a D2O solution of the host molecule according to Part: Preparation of host molecule aqueous solutions or dispersions.
Calculate the required volume of the D2O solution of the host molecule.
Prepare the aqueous solution of the guest molecule according to the specified protocol.
Prepare the aqueous solution of the host molecule according to the specified protocol.
Mix the two aqueous solutions in different molar ratios to form hierarchical host-guest supramolecular self-assemblies.
Determine the critical aggregate concentration (CAC) for hierarchical host-guest supramolecular self-assemblies.
Prepare a solution of hierarchical host-guest supramolecular self-assemblies and leave standing for more than 1 hour.
Wash the wafer with acetone and dry it before use.
Place the prepared solution on a dry sliced wafer.
Wash all vessels with filtered deionized water.
Leave the hierarchical host-guest supramolecular self-assemblies solution standing for more than 1 hour before preparing TEM samples.
Drop sample onto gilder TEM grids slowly, ensuring front side of TEM grid is up and covered by carbon film.
Place a filter paper under gilder TEM grids to keep the sample clean.
Use 5-10 μl of solution per gilder TEM grid for sample preparation.
Put gilder TEM grid with carbon film face up.
Handle the grid carefully to avoid damaging the surface.
Set the gilder TEM grids with sample in a dark environment at 25°C for one night.
Place the grid into a standard TEM holder.
Insert the TEM holder into the specimen storehouse.
Find self-assemblies from the sample using low multiplier lens.
Take photos of the samples using high multiplier lens.
Adjust and rearrange the photos in Microsoft PowerPoint for normalization.
